key_insight: An MLIP-assisted CALPHAD workflow can rapidly identify spinodal regions in high-dimensional alloy composition space and predict the resulting microstructure morphology using analytic thermodynamic derivatives.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster alloy design by screening composition-dependent stability and morphology before costly experiments, with coherent strain effects included for more realistic engineering predictions.
method: Train MLIP-based models to obtain thermodynamic and elastic inputs for alloy compositions.
Use analytically derived Gibbs energy Hessians for efficient spinodal stability analysis.
Run elasto-chemical phase-field simulations to visualize microstructure evolution and morphology.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on the Hf-Nb-Ti-V quaternary system, showing high-throughput stability analysis and phase-field prediction in a realistic alloy design setting.
watch_item: The workflow depends on the accuracy and transferability of MLIP and CALPHAD inputs, so predictions may be sensitive to model quality outside the trained composition range.
paper_title: From MLIPs to Microstructure: A High-Throughput Computational Framework to Design Spinodal Alloys in High-Dimensional Composition Spaces via Analytic Derivatives of CALPHAD Model Predictions
